claims.title: Exact cumulative fixed-cost optimum under bounded total-variation source drift
claims.scope: finite rational source laws, one fixed finite rational state-cost vector, finite horizon T, and per-step TV drift bound eta
assumptions: q_0 equals the declared nominal prior p
the same state-cost vector is used at every period
the exact TV mass-transport extremizers are continued in their canonical donor-recipient order as radius grows
nonclaims: the equality is not asserted for a time-varying state-cost vector whose maximizing transport order may change
the theorem does not infer that an empirical source satisfies the declared drift bound

claims.title: Exact bounded static zero-error prefix-code optimization under TV source drift
claims.scope: one finite confusion graph, one rational nominal prior, one rational per-step TV drift bound, finite horizon, and one deterministic codebook fixed for the whole horizon
assumptions: the bounded deterministic code universe exhausts proper independent-set partitions and complete binary prefix shapes below explicit caps
simplex-vertex scenarios make Pareto pruning equivalent to componentwise state-length dominance
the fixed-cost drift theorem applies independently to each surviving code
nonclaims: the result does not optimize adaptive code switching or learning from realized source observations
expected code length is not identified with queueing delay or parent-substrate resource cost

claims.title: Statistical TV uncertainty and declared source drift combine by triangle inequality
claims.scope: a valid TV confidence radius around an empirical training law plus a separately declared TV bound from the training law to a current source law
nonclaims: the declared drift budget D does not acquire statistical coverage merely by being added to a statistical radius
the result does not provide a confidence process for arbitrary nonstationarity

claims.title: Skew K4 static-code drift phase boundary is eta_c(T)=1/[2(T+1)]
claims.scope: complete graph K4, nominal prior (7/10,1/10,1/10,1/10), one static deterministic prefix tree, and finite horizon T
assumptions: the compared nominally optimal unbalanced tree has lengths (1,2,3,3) with the length-one leaf on the dominant state
the exact bounded code search confirms no third deterministic code improves the declared instances
nonclaims: the phase threshold is specific to the declared source and zero-error prefix-code model
the phase change is a decision-theoretic code switch rather than a physical phase transition

claims.title: Bounded exact TV drift-path and static-code audit
claims.scope: the rational K4 path, horizon phase, zero-drift endpoint, and confidence-plus-drift instances exercised by the repository
assumptions: all configured deterministic code and TV transport searches complete below their caps
every explicit extremal path is checked period by period for the declared TV step bound
nonclaims: bounded test agreement is not a runtime scalability theorem
CI success is not used as a substitute for the explicit mathematical path certificate
